title: A closed fibre point with no other fibre generalization is quasi-finite
statement: Let $g:Y\to T$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $y\in Y$ and $t=g(y)$, and identify the underlying space of the fibre $Y_t$ with $g^{-1}(\{t\})$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Suppose that $\{y\}$ is closed in $Y_t$ and that for every $y^{\prime}\in Y_t$, the condition $y\in\overline{\{y^{\prime}\}}$ (closure in $Y_t$) implies $y^{\prime}=y$. Then $g$ is quasi-finite at $y$ [pqf-def-quasifinite].

source.place: Tag 01TH, morphisms-lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize, implication (3) to (1), statement and proof.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R$ about $t$. By the affine-cover definition of locally finite type, choose an affine member $U=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of the cover of $g^{-1}(V)$ containing $y$, with $A$ finitely generated over $R$. Write $\mathfrak p\subset R$ and $\mathfrak q\subset A$ for $t$ and $y$, and set $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $B=A\otimes_R k$. If $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ generate $A$ over $R$, then $a_1\otimes1,\ldots,a_n\otimes1$ generate $B$ over $k$: expand each first tensor factor as a polynomial and absorb its coefficients into the second factor.

source.place: Tag 01TH, lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize, proof of (3) to (1), affine reduction; finite generation after tensoring written explicitly.

proof.text: By the fibre homeomorphism, the subspace $U\cap Y_t=g^{-1}(\{t\})\cap U$ identifies with $\operatorname{Spec}B$. Let $b$ be the prime corresponding to $y$. Closedness of $\{y\}$ restricts to this subspace, so $\{b\}$ is closed. If $b\in\overline{\{b^{\prime}\}}$ in $\operatorname{Spec}B$, the corresponding point $y^{\prime}$ has $y\in\overline{\{y^{\prime}\}}$ in $Y_t$: closure in a subspace is its intersection with ambient closure. The hypothesis gives $y^{\prime}=y$, hence $b^{\prime}=b$. Thus $\{b\}$ is stable under generalization.

source.place: Tag 01TH, lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize, proof of (3) to (1), passage to the affine fibre ring.

proof.text: The spectrum of $k$ has one point, so it is Noetherian. Apply the finite-type Noetherian-spectrum theorem to $k\to B$, using the generators of step 1, to obtain that $\operatorname{Spec}B$ is Noetherian. The Noetherian-space clause of the constructible-subset node now says every finite union of locally closed subsets is constructible. In particular the closed singleton $\{b\}$ is constructible.

source.place: Tag 005L, lemma-constructible-Noetherian-space; Noetherianity supplied by the cited finite-type-spectrum theorem.

proof.text: Apply the constructible-generalization criterion to the commutative ring $B$ and $E=\{b\}$. Constructibility was proved in step 3 and stability under generalization in step 2; therefore $\{b\}$ is open in $\operatorname{Spec}B$.

The prime $b$ contracts to $\mathfrak q$ under $A\to B$, by the specified fibre homeomorphism. Its open singleton is exactly the affine definition of quasi-finiteness of $R\to A$ at $\mathfrak q$. Together with finite type from step 1 and the affine neighbourhoods $y\in U$, $t\in V$, $g(U)\subseteq V$, this supplies the witnesses in the definition that $g$ is quasi-finite at $y$.

source.place: Tag 01TH, lemma-quasi-finite-at-point-characterize, conclusion of (3) to (1); Tag 01TD and Algebra Tag 00PL, affine definitions.
